_comment: The Turnkey OPERATOR profile — one per Turnkey instance (per franchisee). This is the ONLY file a white-label operator must replace: the engine, gates, consent log, and agents are all brand-agnostic and read the operator's identity from here. This file = instance #1 (Vision Outreach Media, the franchisor dogfooding its own product).

operator.name: Vision Outreach Media
operator.tagline: We launch and run a turnkey business for you — and it is genuinely yours.
operator.voice: Mission-driven, plain-spoken, trust-first, and (for the church niche) faith-friendly. Never hype, never jargon. Speak like a helpful expert, not a salesperson. Deliverables say "Vision Outreach Media (VOM)" or "the operator" — never a personal name.
operator.niche_focus: churches / faith-based organizations (VOM's specialization; not a constraint of the tool)

brand.note: The operator's HOUSE brand. An individual launched business may carry its own product brand (e.g. the church AI-assessment uses a liturgical violet/gold system); this house brand is the default and the franchisor identity.

platform.note: The operator's provisioned rails. These back the generic gate-matrix keys in launch-state.json; agents read the concrete values from here when a workstream needs them.
platform.registrar: one.com (legacy — apex + existing owned domains only, frozen for new client domains)
platform.registrar_wholesale: Openprovider Membership Basic S — the account NEW client domains are registered through, at registry cost, with the CLIENT as registrant and VOM as admin/tech contact. No markup; transfer-out free and unconditional (rail D4). Decision + signup runbook: vom-systems/domains/registrar-decision.md. STATUS: account not yet provisioned.
platform.stripe: VOM platform account (operator-run = direct charges; Connect Express is for client tenants)
platform.wordpress_hosting: one.com managed WordPress (VOM's own apex); client WordPress sites are hosted per-client and DNS-pointed from the delegated clients zone
platform.wordpress_capability: VOM ships the Engage AI WordPress plugin — on a WordPress site the owner gets the Content Studio, publishing and ground-truth analytics inside their own wp-admin. This is a tie-breaker advantage, not a reason to force WordPress on a business that structurally needs an application.
platform._blueprint_note: cms_default / wordpress_capability feed the deterministic site-platform decision in engine/blueprints.py. A franchisee without a WordPress product should set cms_default to "custom" and drop wordpress_capability.

gate_matrix_status.note: Optional per-operator overrides for the one-time-ever bootstrap prereqs. `init` seeds a fresh business's gate matrix from these so business #2+ inherits what business #1 cleared. Omit a key to leave it 'pending'.
